title_en: Lookout: Industry News and Press Review
title_ru: Lookout: Новости индустрии и обзор прессы
meta_description_en: Computer industry news and UK magazine review: Datel acquisitions, Amstrad updates, MGT universal drive, and highlights from Computer Shopper, Sinclair User, and Your Sinclair.
meta_description_ru: Новости компьютерного рынка и обзор британской прессы: поглощения Datel, новости Amstrad и MGT, а также обзор свежих номеров Computer Shopper, Sinclair User и Your Sinclair.
body_en_plain:
Last year you may remember, RAM
Electronics took over DK'Tronics
but now Datel have taken over
them both!Perhaps an even bigger
fish will swim along next year.

Amstrad are going to bundle some
games, a joystick and a light
gun with the Spectrum +2 and +3
in the next few months. Alan
Sugar has obviously had his eye
on the (modest) success of the
ST with its "free" software. It
would be nicer if he included a
cassette lead and a printer lead

as standard as well as the MGT
fixer and other essentials.

Speaking of MGT - they are to
produce a "lifetime" disc drive
which, with the right cable,will
work on many systems (the idea
being that when you upgrade to a
new computer you can still use
the same drive in the same way
that you can still use the same
printer). At present the drive
works with the Spectrum(and +D),
BBC, ST, QL, Amiga and PC.

I heard that POPULAR COMPUTING
WEEKLY was voted No.1 computer
magazine in a survey by Computer
Trade Weekly. Did anyone see the
original report in CTW? If so,
I'd appreciate fuller details.

Further to our report in April's
issue that Amstrad "only" made
`75 million profit during the
previous 6 months, Amstrad have
now announced they expect their
profits to be down during the
present 6 month period too. City
analysts who had previously
predicted a profit of around
`190 million now think profits
will be nearer `100 million. I
feel really, really sorry for
poor old Amstrad - not satisfied
with mere high speed - they seem
to want unending acceleration!

Let's see what's in this month's
computer magazines...

CRASH was not available in time
for our deadline AGAIN! - Sorry!

COMPUTER SHOPPER has a review of
the new 24-pin flat-bed printer
from C. Itoh; their excellent
general programming section has
a look at debugging principles;
SINCLAIR SCENE has an extensive
review of MIRA FORTRAN for the
Spectrum; the artificial intell-
igence section looks at neural
networks and what can be learned
from the way the brain works and
they are still running a regular
glossary of terminology.COMPUTER
EXPRESS WEEKLY also publish the
successive parts of an alphabet-
ical dictionary of computer
expressions so if you get either
you can compile a comprehensive
work of reference.(and I thought
grey scale meant dandruff and a
nanosecond was a fast assembly
line for Mary Poppins dolls).

SINCLAIR USER has an article on
some of the maths involved in
programming a pinball game. SU
still refer to Andrew Hewson in
a vague sort of way in this part
of the magazine yet the text
does not have his style. He's
such a big-name personality in
Spectrum software that it's
puzzling why they dropped his
name (and picture) from the
prominence it used to have.

YOUR SINCLAIR has a 2nd-hand
buyer's guide which is a useful
reference and reminder of both
prices and specification of the
different Spectrums. YS also has
a listing for a routine that
will convert machine code into
BASIC DATA statements in hex

format for POKEing back into
memory. This sounds a bit like
one of the routines in TK50 in
OUTLET Issue 11 but this created
decimal DATA in numeric form.The
YS routine creates hex as string
DATA I think. The latest version
of the SWIFTDISC interface is
also reviewed.

                       - Brian.

                       - Brian.
body_en:
## Lookout

Last year you may remember, RAM Electronics took over DK'Tronics but now Datel have taken over them both! Perhaps an even bigger fish will swim along next year.

Amstrad are going to bundle some games, a joystick and a light gun with the Spectrum +2 and +3 in the next few months. Alan Sugar has obviously had his eye on the (modest) success of the ST with its "free" software. It would be nicer if he included a cassette lead and a printer lead as standard as well as the MGT fixer and other essentials.

Speaking of MGT — they are to produce a "lifetime" disc drive which, with the right cable, will work on many systems (the idea being that when you upgrade to a new computer you can still use the same drive in the same way that you can still use the same printer). At present the drive works with the Spectrum (and +D), BBC, ST, QL, Amiga and PC.

I heard that POPULAR COMPUTING WEEKLY was voted No.1 computer magazine in a survey by Computer Trade Weekly. Did anyone see the original report in CTW? If so, I'd appreciate fuller details.

Further to our report in April's issue that Amstrad "only" made £75 million profit during the previous 6 months, Amstrad have now announced they expect their profits to be down during the present 6 month period too. City analysts who had previously predicted a profit of around £190 million now think profits will be nearer £100 million. I feel really, really sorry for poor old Amstrad — not satisfied with mere high speed — they seem to want unending acceleration!

Let's see what's in this month's computer magazines...

CRASH was not available in time for our deadline AGAIN! — Sorry!

COMPUTER SHOPPER has a review of the new 24-pin flat-bed printer from C. Itoh; their excellent general programming section has a look at debugging principles; SINCLAIR SCENE has an extensive review of MIRA FORTRAN for the Spectrum; the artificial intelligence section looks at neural networks and what can be learned from the way the brain works and they are still running a regular glossary of terminology. COMPUTER EXPRESS WEEKLY also publish the successive parts of an alphabetical dictionary of computer expressions so if you get either you can compile a comprehensive work of reference. (and I thought grey scale meant dandruff and a nanosecond was a fast assembly line for Mary Poppins dolls).

SINCLAIR USER has an article on some of the maths involved in programming a pinball game. SU still refer to Andrew Hewson in a vague sort of way in this part of the magazine yet the text does not have his style. He's such a big-name personality in Spectrum software that it's puzzling why they dropped his name (and picture) from the prominence it used to have.

YOUR SINCLAIR has a 2nd-hand buyer's guide which is a useful reference and reminder of both prices and specification of the different Spectrums. YS also has a listing for a routine that will convert machine code into BASIC DATA statements in hex format for POKEing back into memory. This sounds a bit like one of the routines in TK50 in OUTLET Issue 11 but this created decimal DATA in numeric form. The YS routine creates hex as string DATA I think. The latest version of the SWIFTDISC interface is also reviewed.

— Brian.
body_ru:
## Lookout: Новости индустрии

В прошлом году, как вы помните, RAM Electronics поглотила DK'Tronics, но теперь Datel поглотила их обеих! Возможно, в следующем году приплывёт рыба и покрупнее.

Amstrad собирается в ближайшие пару месяцев класть в комплект со Spectrum +2 и +3 игры, джойстик и световой пистолет. Alan Sugar, очевидно, положил глаз на (скромный) успех ST с его «бесплатным» софтом. Было бы куда лучше, если бы он включил в стандартную комплектацию провод для кассетника и кабель принтера, а также фикс для MGT и прочие необходимые мелочи.

К слову об MGT — они собираются выпустить дисковод «на всю жизнь», который с нужным кабелем будет работать на многих системах (идея в том, что при апгрейде на новый компьютер вы сможете использовать тот же привод точно так же, как используете тот же принтер). Сейчас этот дисковод работает со Spectrum (и +D), BBC, ST, QL, Amiga и PC.

Я слышал, что POPULAR COMPUTING WEEKLY признали компьютерным журналом №1 по результатам опроса Computer Trade Weekly. Кто-нибудь видел оригинальную заметку в CTW? Если да, буду рад любым подробностям.

В продолжение нашего апрельского сообщения о том, что прибыль Amstrad составила «всего» `75 million за предыдущие полгода: Amstrad объявила, что ожидает падения прибыли и в текущем полугодии. Аналитики из Сити, ранее предрекавшие прибыль около `190 million, теперь считают, что она будет ближе к `100 million. Мне искренне, искренне жаль беднягу Amstrad: мало им просто высокой скорости — подавай им вечное ускорение!

Посмотрим, что пишут в журналах в этом месяце...

CRASH СНОВА не успел выйти к нашему дедлайну! Извините!

В COMPUTER SHOPPER есть обзор нового 24-игольчатого планшетного принтера от C. Itoh; их отличный общий раздел по программированию разбирает принципы отладки; в SINCLAIR SCENE — подробный обзор MIRA FORTRAN для Spectrum; в разделе об искусственном интеллекте рассматриваются нейросети и то, чему можно научиться у работы мозга, а также продолжается регулярный глоссарий терминов. COMPUTER EXPRESS WEEKLY тоже публикует по частям алфавитный словарь компьютерных терминов, так что читая любой из них, можно собрать отличный справочник (а я-то думал, что grey scale — это перхоть, а наносекунда — скоростной конвейер кукол Mary Poppins).

В SINCLAIR USER есть статья о математике, необходимой при программировании пинбола. В этом разделе SU до сих пор как-то смутно ссылаются на Andrew Hewson, хотя стиль текста совсем не его. Он такая известная личность в мире софта для Spectrum, что просто непонятно, почему его имя (и фото) перестали красоваться на самом видном месте, как раньше.

В YOUR SINCLAIR напечатан гид по покупке б/у техники — полезный справочник и напоминание о ценах и характеристиках разных моделей Spectrum. Ещё в YS есть листинг процедуры, переводящей машинный код в операторы DATA Бейсика в шестнадцатеричном формате для последующего POKE в память. Это похоже на одну из процедур TK50 из OUTLET Issue 11, но та делала десятичные DATA в числовом виде. Процедура из YS, кажется, делает hex в виде строковых DATA. Также там есть обзор свежей версии интерфейса SWIFTDISC.

*— Brian.*
